utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. May we have the appearances, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Teresa McHenry for the Prosecution appearing with Mr. Turone and Ms. Udo. Mr. Niemann should be joining us later this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Edina Residovic, the Defence counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic, along with my colleague Mr. Eugene O'Sullivan, a professor from Canada. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Zeljko Olujic, Defence counsel for Mr. Zdravko Mucic, along with my colleague Mr. Tomislav Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Salih Karabdic, attorney from Sarajevo, Defence counsel for Mr. Hazim Delic, along with Mr. Thomas Moran, attorney from Houston, Texas. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Nancy Boler. I represent Esad Landzo. Cynthia McMurrey is still in the United States at the funeral. I'm joined this morning by David Eisen. David is my law partner in Houston who has been approved by the registry as a legal assistant. He will be here today and tomorrow before he goes back to Houston.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. EISEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we invite the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I address you for half a minute before the witness is brought back in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Just a minute. Let's see what the subject matter is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have been thinking about your comments yesterday regarding the presentation of evidence for the Defence, and I would just like to advise you that we have done everything to prepare witnesses for these proceedings. We have two or three witnesses who were very important personalities in Konjic during the period of war, and we have prepared a number of documents with respect to these witnesses. We beg your indulgence in presenting a larger number of documents through these couple of witnesses, and we are fully aware of the time constrictions, but we would like just to give you a prior warning that we have these witnesses, and we beg your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I hear your plea, but, you know, in every Prosecution or Defence, evidence is led in accordance with the Defence strategy and in answer to the accusations against the accused persons. Now, when evidence, even in answer of an accusation, is put repeatedly and, to some extent, irrelevant, it is the duty of the Trial Chamber to reject them. Now, if you are assuming from your own side that, perhaps, a particular person is very important, merely because of his station in the community or his importance to you, it might still not be the fact that it enables us to establish the truth in accordance with the accusations against the accused. The real duty of the Trial Chamber is to determine what is relevant, not merely because it is repetitive or duplicating, or not merely because counsel thinks it's his duty to present him. As far as we're concerned, we do not think it is right in the interest of justice and in the interest of effectiveness of the trial. Above all, not merely because the Tribunal is paying the cost, it is unfair and does not, frankly, assist the integrity of counsel who is presenting it, that is competent to project and defend the accused who are standing trial, because the Trial Chamber relies on the integrity of counsel and their competence. But if the evidence which is led exposes to the Trial Chamber that what is being done is not competent, it is our duty as Trial Judges to reject it. This is what I believe we intend to do. I've heard what you said, and as we proceed, we'll decide what to do. Let the witness come in.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel for Mr. Landzo please turn off her microphone?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is a technical problem that we are facing right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Why are we having these technical problems on a daily basis? We should try to check this before. Kindly inform the witness that --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, my apologies to you. I actually do not have a socket available to plug myself in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's strange because you should have one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I ask for someone's assistance, please, so that we can get the right jack so we can get plugged in?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Edina can use mine and we will share until one is available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your assistance. Please inform the witness he is still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness may not have heard the registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I do not get the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Check his own headphones, whether they are on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is all right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, have you heard now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you understand the advice that you are still under oath, sir? Very well. MIDHAT CEROVAC

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, yesterday we talked about the departure of the Gajret unit from Konjic which, in Pazaric, was subordinated to Mr. Polutak who was commander of Tactical Group 1. Mr. Cerovac, did Mr. Delalic have any kind of command duty in relationship to that unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Delalic, at that time, have any kind of command position in the Territorial Defence of the Konjic municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you present at the ceremony of the send-off of this unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I play you a videotape, I am going to then ask you whether you can recognise it. Can the technical booth please play the videotape, excerpt 1?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please fast forward through this portion? Can you now please slow down? Please fast forward for a bit longer. This could be fast forwarded. Now please go for half a minute go slow.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, watching this videotape, do you know who is in prison in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Babo (phoen).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What do you have to do to liberate Babo?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could the technical booth please stop here?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, do you know what event is presented on this videotape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This event shown here was the send-off of the unit, which we established pursuant to the order of the superior command in Sarajevo, and it was to be subordinated to the Tactical Group 1 in Pazaric and Mr. Polutak was the commander of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cerovac. Since you have already testified that at this time, Mr. Delalic had no commanding role, what was his role at this send-off ceremony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you will recall, I think I already stated this yesterday, Mr. Delalic, through his own connections and acquaintances, managed to equip this unit with uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, we have already heard that. I'm just asking what his role was at the send-off of this unit. Was he there in an honorary position or did he have a military position there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely no military position because at the morning briefing, we agreed, due to the efforts which he invested in equipping the unit, so we agreed to let him speak to the members of this unit as part of the ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cerovac. The Trial Chamber has already seen this material and Mr. Delalic addressed the soldiers with Salam Haleikoum. Can you tell us what kind of greeting this is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You can take this as a greeting from one Muslim to another Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is exactly what the witness is going to testify to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this what one soldier -- how one soldier addresses another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The greeting Salam Aleikoum is something used by all Muslims around the world.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In these specific circumstances, was this a civilian greeting civilians, or was it a soldier greeting civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was a simple greeting of one soldier to another and one civilian to another. He used it throughout.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I think that we are done with this excerpt and I think that the technical booth can remove it. Mr. Cerovac, were you asked by the Brigadier Vejzagic to draft certain charts for his expert opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that in late '97 and early '98, I met Mr. Vejzagic for the first time, and I told him that I would endeavour to compile all necessary documents and maps and charts for his expert report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness now please be shown the Defence Exhibit 145 and annex 5D/2?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Please, could you repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: 5D/2, which is number 689 and 690 of the English and Bosnian text respectively.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, please place the Bosnian text in front of you, and if you could please place the English translation on the ELMO so that the Trial Chamber could follow what we are about to talk about. Mr. Cerovac, is this the chart which you drafted for Brigadier Vejzagic, that is, for his expert report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As you can see in the lower right corner, I even signed it. This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, according to your knowledge, does this chart reflect the organisation of defence in Konjic in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is for the period April through October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What year? 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To whom were the combat units in Konjic subordinate, that is, the units which you specified in the lower part of your chart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a complete chart. Also, the system of control and command is also represented here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What type of lines did you use to show the control and command lines? Did you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the legend, this is the full line with the arrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, it is not necessary to go into the further explaining of this chart, it is enough that you have confirmed that you compiled it. Your Honours, I tender this chart since it has been authenticated by the witness. Would you please tell me what is the exhibit of the Defence? What is the next number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It has been admitted as it has been marked, D145 annex 5D/2/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could the witness now please be shown, and I would like the usher's assistance, this is the Defence Exhibit 145 and then it's 5D/5 and the numbers are 694 and, I believe, 695. Mr. Cerovac, I would also will like to ask you if you could place the Bosnian version of the chart in front of you and if you could place the English version on the ELMO. Mr. Cerovac, did you personally draft this chart at the request of Ms. Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this organisational chart of the municipal headquarters reflect the actual structure of the municipal headquarters in 1992, that is, at the time when you were first a member of and then the chief of the municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, could you show us where your position was in the headquarters, based on this chart? If you can just point at your position on the chart, which is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My position is in this rubric where it says "staff" and then the "chief of staff."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As the witness has identified this document and this document has previously been admitted, I am just going to confirm that the witness has authenticated this document. Can the witness now be shown D145, annex 5D/10? Mr. Cerovac, is this also another chart which you drafted in 1998 for the expert report of Mr. Vacagic (phoen)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what this chart represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a chart reflecting the structure which shows the organisational chart of the joint command of the Territorial Defence and the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show me your position in this chart? And if you could please do that on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My position is right here. It is an officer for operations and training and this is the duty that I discharged at the time. I was also on duty shown in the box above. This is assistant commander for chief of staff for operations and training.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This chart, which has been admitted before, has now been authenticated by the person who actually drafted it. Mr. Cerovac, can you tell me whether there were certain minor changes which took place during this period of time with respect to the chart as you have drafted it here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first changes which took place, were those pertaining to the commander of this joint command. This is Mr. Ramic and Mr. Boric. Further changes occurred in the operations and training sector, and I already stated what those were. There was also a change in the security body.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that this is sufficient, so there were some minor changes there. Could you tell me who was assistant commander for security in a joint command? The member of which part of the joint forces occupied that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was appointed to that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a man from Konjic was appointed to that position. He was an attorney by profession. He was the chief of public security station before the aggression and his name was Mr. Goran Lokas.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, during this period when the joint command was in existence, was the position of the assistant commander for security always going to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this period, who could appoint as a member of the Prad (phoen) ethnic group to command positions in a staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean this, for this staff, this staff of joint command?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was exclusively the HVO. That is, the chief of staff, Dinko Zebic, who was also the commander of the HVO units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We saw the charts which you drafted. Can you tell me, based on that, was, at any point in time in 1992, Zejnil Delalic a member of the municipal staff of the joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not in practice, not in theory.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, during 1992, did Mr. Delalic have any position, any command position, in the municipal headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, at no time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the period when the joint command was in existence, was Mr. Delalic on duty as a member of the joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, at any time. As you can tell, he's not present on this chart at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could a person be in a command position in the staff or the joint command without being appointed to such a duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at all. This cannot happen in any military organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, could you tell us, during the period of time when the joint command was in existence, how were the orders of the joint command issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The orders of the joint command were issued whenever there was common interest involved, that is, when there was a consensus between the commanders of the joint command and the chief of staff of the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who signed such orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of the joint command and the chief of staff of the joint command. And if one of them, if the commander of the joint command was absent, it would be a person whom he would authorise from the ranks of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, how were appointments made in this period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All appointments were done separately because there was a dual command at a time. That is, appointments in the structures of the Territorial Defence at all levels of the units whose commander was the commander of the Territorial Defence and all appointments in the joint command, that is, at a level of the HVO's headquarters. That means both at the level of units and headquarters was done by the commander of the HVO units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Cerovac. I think you have explained that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And he himself was appointed by the headquarters at Grude.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your position of the operations officer and assistant commander for operations and training, were you in a position to work on preparation of documents regarding, the combat operations of the municipal staff and of the joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was a member of the body, which was preparing all significant documents so regarding planning and carrying out of combat operations and proposed to the commander -- which were proposed to the commander and to the chief of staff of the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, I am now going to show you several documents, so please tell me whether you can recognise these documents which were compiled at the joint TO, HVO command? These are documents which have previously been offered through the expert report. I am just going to show you for authentication, I have enough copies for the trial chamber and the Prosecutor. Let me give you the numbers. These are the following documents: D-145 Annex 5D/11. D-145 D/21. D-145 Annex 5D/15. D-145 Annex 5D/17. And D-144 Annex 5B. Could all of these documents be given to the witness together so that he could answer the question. Mr. Cerovac, will you please review these documents? Mr. Cerovac, is it correct that all these documents were signed both by the commander of the joint command, who was the commander of the TO, and the chief of staff of the joint command, who was also the commander of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Working in the joint command, as somebody who worked there, could you confirm for the Trial Chamber that these documents were, indeed, documents which were compiled in the joint command headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, these are documents which support the expert report and the witness has recognised them as those that were compiled at the joint command, so I offer them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honours, with respect to at least two of them, I notice that the documents were incomplete and appear to have been altered or redacted. Given that they are not the actual documents and have been altered, we certainly would object to their admission for any purposes. If Ms. Residovic is able to supply us with unaltered versions, then we may withdraw our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is it really important, giving instances of orders being signed by commanders of both forces? Do they have any real bearing on the case?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: If Your Honours were not to let them into evidence at all because they were irrelevant, then certainly then, we wouldn't object. But if they are going to be admitted at all, because they are relevant, we certainly think, for one, we may want to do our own looking into whether these are authentic documents and their relevance. We certainly would be unable to do that if the documents have been altered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is an admitted position that some of these documents have been signed by both. Even some of the documents, produced by the prosecution itself shows, that some of the orders have been signed by the commanders of the HVO as a letter to you. Why do you bring them to the court unnecessarily? They don't have any bearing on the guilt or innocence of your client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What do you want to establish by them being admitted? The documents could be signed by both commanders as joint commanders. That's all you're trying to show.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You have already said, your witness, that Mr. Delalic did not occupy any position in the TO or the joint command or in the HVO. So that should be the end of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: One of these documents, which is document concerning the attack on Bradina, has already been admitted, but what these documents show, they show the method of commanding during the period when Mr. Zejnil Delalic was not there. This witness was preparing these documents for his commander, Zerabic (phoen) and Boric. This all shows that Mr. Delalic was not involved in either issuing orders or appointing persons to duties. In that respect, I find that this document is relevant and the witness is someone who has actually prepared them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Not a member of the TO at that time. He was never, and there were already commanders in those places. He could not also be a commander. So how can it be relevant when, in fact, he played no part in any of these proceedings at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: According to this witness, when the attack on Bradina took place, Delalic was in Zagreb, this is what he said, he couldn't have possibly taken part in this operation. That is what this witness said yesterday. How are these documents relevant? You're unnecessarily calling on something which is not bearing on the --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They confirm the credibility, both of this witness and other witnesses, because these are not just words. There are documents to support these words and this goes directly to what the Prosecution has been arguing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Then they support nothing. The moment that they disputed; they support nothing. So when, in fact, the words which have not been challenged, the evidence of the witness has not been challenged and other witnesses have not been challenged, why are you introducing a disputed document?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe we can bring it up again in a status conference. What I'm trying to do is really follow your instructions. There was an expert witness who could not speak to the documents. He had not compiled them. He could not authenticate them and now we have a witness who actually did compile these documents, so now I asked him whether he can recognise these documents, whether he can authenticate it. This is all I wanted of this witness. If Your Honours see that it is sufficient that is enough that these documents were compiled by the joint command, I don't need to go any further. This is how I see these documents. I think that it helps determine the position of my clients, as well as the situation as it was on the ground in Konjic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, was Mr. Zejnil Delalic at any period of time in 1992, in a position to sign as a member of either the headquarters or the joint command, any orders or appointments which were binding to you as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I personally as a soldier was bound by orders coming from two distinct levels. It is the level of a commander and the level of the superior command in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. Your client did sign a few orders along with the commanders of the HVO and the TO.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Your client did sign some orders along with the commander of the HVO and the TO and he described himself as a commander, although he also said -- the orders also said that he was signing as coordinator. If there's any explanation which this witness can offer, please ask him about it, otherwise, this document is really not relevant, because if you believe that he had nothing to do with the TO, he had nothing to do with the HVO, then these orders become irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is correct that we have seen documents which my client has signed as a coordinator, but my client never described himself as a commander, and I don't think that we had any documents showing that, but let me turn to the witness now and try to clarify that with him right away.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If there was a document which was signed by the commander or the commander of the HVO additionally and there was also a coordinator signing it, did that mean that the coordinator was the one who was also issuing you this command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely not. The orders which were binding for us, for me as a member of the Territorial Defence, were only the orders which came from my own commander or the commander of the joint command, as well as orders which I received from the chief of staff of the joint command. In certain cases, if such documents existed, the coordinator was, his signature figured on certain documents only as a witness to certain events because frequently, certain orders were not carried out, that is, certain actions that were set out in certain documents were combined actions, which means certain actions that involved civilian aspects which were of special significance and actions where the involvement of the military was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cerovac. Perhaps I will show you some of the documents that would further clarify this issue further on, where in some of the orders signed by commanders, there is also a signature of the coordinator. Mr. Cerovac, during 1992 and before you became the brigade commander, did you ever substitute for the commander or did you act on his behalf?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether as an acting commander, did you also carry out certain actions that had to do with control and command, in other words, did you issue orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I always knew at the morning briefing whether the commander was going to be present or not, whether he was going to visit the front-lines, and he would always issue me orders orally so that I would actually sign all the documents that were very urgent on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the commander was absent due to being wounded or something else, did you have authority, were you given authority as a commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The first such case happened during the operation at Borci.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the first case of a longer period of time, you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was during the operation at Borci.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regardless of whether you substituted for the commander for a shorter or longer period of time, was at any of these times, Mr. Delalic a person who could issue commands or make appointments of any kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not in practise, not in theory.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In order to authenticate the documents which are in the expert report, Mr. Cerovac, I'm going to show you certain documents which bear your signature and I want to see whether you can identify these documents. D145, A5. These are copies, if necessary, to remind the Trial Chamber. D145, annex D5/40. D145, AD/27; D145, AD/28; D145, A9/9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We are the only ones without these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While the documents are being distributed to the court, Mr. Cerovac, will you please look at them? I have given a copy for their Honours, but I'm not sure about the order in which they should be distributed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, will you please look at the document of the 25th of July, 1992, order on the appointment to the command of the Ljubinje detachment. Mr. Cerovac, will you please tell me whether you recognise the signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, is that one of the documents which you signed by authority of the commander Esad Ramic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is. You can see, in front, the name of the position and, according to the instructions on office work, it is obligatory to add the word for, for the commander, which means that you have been authorised by him to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cerovac, will you please look at another document with the same date, 25th July, 1992, order on appointment issued to the command of Zupcanik detachment. Do you recognise the signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is an order that I personally drew up and I put my function on it, my title.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are we talking about document 01234/1 of the 25th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is an order on the use of units, deployment of units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, you just mentioned the order on the deployment of units, the document headed the 23rd of July, but my question referred to the document of the 25th of July, 1992, order on appointment issued to the command of Zupcanik detachment. I think there was a small misunderstanding between us. Do you have the document now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you recognise the signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document that you signed by authority of the commander, as is the case for the previous document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you now look at the document that you referred to a moment ago dated the 23rd of July, order on the deployment of units? Were these documents drafted when your commander, due to injury, was absent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. From the middle of July and throughout the second half of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said a moment ago that this is an order on the deployment of a unit. Can you tell me what it actually means, this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This order, I had come from the area of Glavaticevo to Konjic because intelligence information could not reach me through communications and this information had to do with the forces of the aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This may be very important for you, explaining why you came there, but will you tell me why this unit of 90 men were accommodated in the barracks and with what purpose?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The unit was put up in the Celebici barracks, so that it should be equipped with the necessary material in one place, with sufficient quantities of food supplies and rations and for its assignment to be made clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean -- actually, I want to ask you whether in the area of the Celebici barracks, which is a very large compound, were units of the Territorial Defence put up there during preparations for combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please now look at the document of the 21st of September, 1992? Do you recognise the signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now look at the document dated 3rd June, 1992. Tell me who signed, standing in for the commander of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did as can clearly be seen by my legible signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, as you see, this is one of the documents on which the signature of Zejnil Delalic figures. Tell me, does this signature mean that Zejnil Delalic is issuing this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to your understanding of things and according to your experience and the rules, who issued this order? Or to be more precise, who are the persons who issued this order, as far as you are concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that Zejnil Delalic is not a person issuing orders. For a soldier, who is the author of this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exclusively the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, using this as an example, as you, yourself, signed this document, what was the task of Zejnil Delalic, according to the provisions of this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zejnil Delalic, upon the proposal of the economics staff, was tasked to coordinate activities between the representative of the railway station in Konjic, Mr. Vesiko Bunjic (phoen) and a representative of the armed structures. His principal task was, to set in motion the railway line between Jablanica and Pazaric, which was of particular significance for three municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. No, please proceed. You were going to add something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the task of the army was to provide combat security of that train.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know personally whether Zejnil Delalic accomplished the task assigned to him by this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is common knowledge. That was the first train that started operating in the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina under the control of the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, in fact, I want to know whether this was a task given to Zejnil Delalic or was it something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, that was a task given to Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, as this witness has identified his signatures on all these documents, and as I consider them to be relevant, I tender them into evidence as Defence exhibits. Thank you very much. May I just check with the registry? These documents have been entered into the record and the number under which they were identified; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, they have been admitted under the number they have been marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, I should now like to move on to another area having to do with some of the positions in the staff. Will you tell us what was the function of the headquarters of the Stan (phoen) in the joint command, the Stan being the joint headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the joint command, we had security, security for the command itself, distribution of mail, food for members of the command and protection of the most important facilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell me which of the military structures in the joint command did this Stan command belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It belonged to the HVO because the Territorial Defence staff at that time, while the joint command existed, did not have its own military police formed, and if it had had it, then probably those duties would have been carried out jointly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me, Mr. Cerovac, after the end of this period of May/June, in the development of the Territorial Defence, did the post of coordinator exist, as a stage in the development of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the work of the Territorial Defence, and even to this day, since the formation of the army of the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, there is no such word as a "Stage" or "Phase" nor is there the position of coordinator.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So as not to waste too much time over this, was there a coordinator phase in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, were certain combat operations prepared and carried out within your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the second half of June, we were given orders from our superior command to engage in active combat in the direction of Nevesinje, the aim being to ease the pressure on our forces, which were defending the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that we have discussed this at some length, will you tell me whether all the structures of the joint command participated in these preparations, I mean the TO and the HVO, in the preparations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The situation was rather special when it comes to the preparation of those combat operations and at the beginning, the members of the Croatian defence council, the HVO, who belonged to the joint command, expressed their readiness to take an active part in these combat operations, saying that they would support us because we lacked logistic support at the time. When I say we, I'm referring to the Territorial Defence units, that they would reinforce us, but an unforeseen development occurred at the very beginning of these operations. They explained to us that it was not in their national interest to engage in combat in other parts of the municipality and that is the capture of the plateau of Nevesinje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Despite that, did the municipal TO staff decide to carry out this combat operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course, because we were not guided by national interests. What we sought to achieve was to liberate the entire territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As I would now go on to another area, perhaps this would be a convenient time for the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the last in this area, but I intend to move on to another area, so perhaps I'm asking whether this would be a convenient time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If that is your last question, we can break at this stage and come back at 12 noon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I hope you are getting to the next stage of your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as I said, I will go on now to another subject. That is, I will no longer be discussing the control and command question that we have covered, prior to the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, the Court already knows that the Town of Konjic was heavily shelled as of the 4th of May. And it is also aware of the events linked to the combat operations and lifting the blockade on the city. After the deblocking of Bradina, did the shelling of Konjic cease?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The shelling of the Town of Konjic stopped when the date in accords was signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All of you in the municipal staff and the joint command who performed certain duties, did you do so under conditions of intensive combat operations in the town of Konjic, that is during the period of daily shelling of the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly. The situation in the Town of Konjic was terrible. The town was a very easy target for both selective and non-selective shelling and the grenades would destroy particular buildings and would inflict casualties.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I shall now ask the technical service to show a segment of the tape used during the testimony of the expert witness and we can ask the witness whether he recognises the conditions in the Town of Konjic. So will you please show us Tape No. 2, Segment 1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Shelling every day, at least in 1992, why do you want to have a picture? That has been a position that has been adopted and admitted, so why further evidence on that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I mean if you see the picture of shelling, it will make much of a difference will it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We can well imagine what shelling will do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is fine with me. If we don't have to show the picture to the witness. But I would you like to admit these tapes into evidence, because on the tapes, you can see what happened and I consider that to be important for your decision. The tape is just support material. The expert witness could not authenticate it. We have the witness here and he can authenticate the tape and it can serve as a basis for establishing the conditions, which are referred to in the indictment. That is the only reason why we wish to show segments of the tape to this witness, so that I should be able to tender it into evidence. Because we have admitted many tapes tendered by the prosecution, so this is a basis for you to have a general idea of the conditions under which all this was happening. That is the only reason I wish to show it to the witness. It will take a minute or two and if he can authenticate it, then I'll be able to tender it into evidence. Because the conditions determine what each individual was able to do or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This, but I think you will try and restrict yourself to the parameters in which you have called a witness to testify. If you looked at the -- in the motion in which you refer to us what he came to is to give a rule of the coordinator and the Tactical Group 1 of the coordinator and the head of the Tactical Group 1 in respect to the, to the activities, this is what he's here to. What I think you are diverting to other areas, which not necessarily affects those things. And I think this is what in enlarging the evidence. There's no point in moving from the area in which actually you called a witness to testify, into areas which perhaps I really want to hear actual testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How relevant is this command responsibility? What does that mean? You're in charge it's my responsibility, yes commander. You have examined this witness on that aspect. --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am expecting the hearing you have announced, but I asked you with precision how we could give you a summary of what the witnesses would be testifying to. And I asked you whether this should be done in an identical way, as the prosecution has done, and you confirmed that and gave me guidelines and that is what I followed. As for the coordinator or, possibly commander, in view of your legal expertise, as well as mine, you know that is very important to establish the facts in order to be able to judge anybody's responsibility, so that is just -- I would like to be able to show it very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you are giving anybody the role and responsibility of air commander, you do not necessarily go into what gives rise to that role and responsibility. Here is a chief of staff. He's within the authorities and knows exactly what rules are granted to the coordinator or the commander of the tactical group. He would know. And these are the things that anybody expects you to lead evidence to. Not whether a place was shelled, or not whether a place was captured. It has nothing to do with his role. When the person who played that role comes up, he will then tell us what actually he did. But the technical guidelines which outline his role, what are applicable, who are in charge of those roles, I couldn't tell us. Because all these are completely irrelevant to what perhaps ending. You would as well tell us people who played football on that day or any other activity or any other activity that might have happened. These are all activities which are concerned with normal operations of the war period. We expect there will be shelling and so do it. And in an incessant manner with no appointed commander of a tactical group. He has to defend the area for which he was assigned. This witness will be able to tell us that. And this is not all the type of manoeuvring you're telling us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Even you assume that Konjic was entirely destroyed or it remained unscathed, who would it affect, his command responsibility? Let's confine ourselves to the case instead of moving into other fields and other areas and, which has no bearing at all on the guilt or innocence of your client.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, you know that my client, according to us, had no position that any one living in that town was conditioned by the situation in the town. If they spend 24 hours collecting dead bodies or repairing roofs, that is important, regardless of who we are talking about, whether it is this witness or somebody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Let us confine yourselves to the Defence, instead of other fields that have no bearing at all on the question before us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, but counts 46 and 47 speak about inhumane conditions and other things. The witness, Kevric, has told you about that. You have to know whether the conditions were identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If he's not giving evidence of human conditions, go ahead ask him or if you have other witness who can do so, ask them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Inhuman conditions. In the camp, not outside in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He has no responsibility for the areas except in the camp, if at all, especially in the way he was charged. His responsibility is limited to what happened in the camp, not outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: In fact you already led evidence showing there were food shortages and no medical supplies were available.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The witness doesn't speak about the shortage of food, maybe there's some lines, people collecting food. But we're talking about what happened inside the camp. Even if Konjic, as I said, was completely destroyed or it remained unscathed, how would it affect the command responsibility of your client? That's all I am saying, confine the evidence to your defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Assuming he has responsibility all over the place. Even that was the case, was he so charged?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There's no evidence at all that my client was responsible. We're trying to explain to you what his activates were and that is why the breadth of the defence is such as it is. I believe that all this is useful for establishing the facts of the case. There's no camp outside of the context, but I would appeal for a status conference as you have suggested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Just the facts of the case. It's none of your business.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's very difficult for me to begin, but if, in the introduction, the prosecution says that the forces attacked a certain village and horrors were happening and you're not aware of them, unless you let me show you, but I will continue with the examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: It's not for your case. Your point is to defend your client. It's for the Prosecutor to prove the facts of the indictment or not to prove them, not for you. That's what my colleagues are trying to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but how can I call in question, the facts presented to the court, and which have been admitted into evidence if I don't give you any counter evidence. How will you be able to view it differently because you have already admitted into evidence, material that are not -- that is not truthful in the position of the Defence. And for the Defence to be able to dispute the evidence tendered by the prosecution, we have to offer other evidence. That evidence has been admitted and I have to cast doubt regarding that evidence. May I ask, rapidly, to be shown the tape with the situation in June and if the court considers it to be irrelevant, the court can reject it. And that is why I am asking the technical booth to show us this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't think it's necessary to show it. Move on with another aspect of your evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, you said that the HVO, a day before the body operation, declined to participate. Tell us please who issued the order for the beginning of the operation Oganj or Borci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was issued and signed by Mr. Esad Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was the commander of that operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Esad Ramic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We also have evidence on that. Esad Ramic (indiscernible). The next man then took over, it was the previous witness before us, on the this Borci operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we remember. This man was for a time the commander of the operation and that is the difference and secondly, I am not accustomed to having a discussion with the Trial Chamber, I have too much respect to be able to enter into any discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We merely point out what has already come on the record. I am not discussing it with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's the evidence we have.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, did you take over command of the Borci operation at a certain point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which were the reasons for you to take over command of that operation; the wounding of commander Ramic, in the area of Tisovica (phoen). This is a mountain chain, part of the Prenj Mountains. This occurred in the first half of July or the middle of July, to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me please did Mr. Zejnil Delalic participate in operation Oganj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He had the role of rank and file soldier. And he was in the area of Mount Zvekusa or more precisely, Vranske Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who worked on the preparatory documents for this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The operations and training department, to which I belonged.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For the needs of this operation, did you form some smaller tactical groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. To facilitate control and command, to facilitate the communications system.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, those tactical groups that are mentioned in your order, do they have anything to do with the Tactical Group based in Pazaric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, tell me, please, how long did this operation last, Operation Oganj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It lasted just over one month until the beginning of August, but certain smaller formations with specific assignments remained in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, during that operation, did Zejnil Delalic receive any kind of command military function during that operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He could not have been given any such assignments, because he was not within the structure of the control and command system.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which were his duties and responsibilities and can you tell us exactly where he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that he had a purely military task, the task of a soldier, a very specific task of providing logistic support from the area of Vranske Stijene or, to be more precise, the village of Dubociri (phoen). Logistic supplies could reach this village by motor car, and his further task was to organise the speedy loading and unloading of the supplies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that the court is familiar with logistic activities. Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the transport which went on from there with the help of horses, on horseback, he had to transport these supplies from the Rakatica Canyon (phoen).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think these details now we don't need to go into. Thank you, Mr. Cerovac. You have told me it is not a command function, but tell me, in the view of the position he had, could he have command over the artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he could not command the artillery. He could convey my demands, my own personal demands. This could be done by him or anyone else with the exact coordinates.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I didn't have good links with the artillery positions on Mount Zvekusa.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Linked to this operation, will you tell me geographically what this area is like, Vranske Stijene, Prajn, in the direction of Lake Borci. In terms of geography, is it mountainous area, inaccessible? Can you just describe it in a couple of sentences for the benefit of the judges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To explain it more graphically, we headed out from the town of Konjic, which has an altitude of about 267 metres, to the mountainous areas of Prenj where the average altitude is about 1,500 metres, and also towards Glavaticevo, where the highest point was about 1,200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because of these problems and communication problems, before the actual operation, did you establish certain relay stations for communications with the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, we had to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have already heard testimony about this. I just wanted you to confirm this fact before the court. We shall now go on to the next area. Mr. Cerovac, do you know whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic was at a certain point in time appointed to a command post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you kindly repeat the question because I cannot hear the translation properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, do you know that Mr. Delalic at one point in time in 1992 became commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This was towards the end of the month of July, perhaps seven days before this operation had ended, he was appointed commander of TG-1. The duty was performed earlier on by Mr. Mustafa Polutak who had a car accident prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever personally meet Mr. Polutak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I met him in Konjic. We met in the motel which is located in the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Polutak a superior to the municipal staff of Konjic at the time you met him or at any other point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He couldn't be in a superior position to the municipal staff. These tactical groups are divided, actually in military warfare adopted by the western bloc --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we have heard the experts on this topic, so I would like to ask you as a witness of these events: Did Mr. Polutak, when you met him or during the time while he was commander, at any point in time, whether he was personally superior to him or to the municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he wasn't, so he couldn't be my superior either.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, you said that at the end of July, Mr. Delalic had become the commander of Tactical Group 1. Can you tell me whether Mr. Delalic, as commander of TG-1 at any point in time while he was discharging that duty, was he your superior or to the municipal staff of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He said no. He has already said that. He has already said no, he was not a superior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Polutak was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He said about Mr. Polutak. I'm talking about Mr. Delalic now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: In that regard, I have another question, but you finish first.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please answer the question: When he became commander of TG-1 in July, was Mr. Delalic, at any moment while he was discharging that duty, whether he was your superior or the superior of the municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he wasn't our superior, nor was Mr. Polutak either, so he couldn't have been my superior or the superior of the municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute, before you proceed further, I have a question to ask of the witness. Can you give this copy to him? This is document 99/7/7, whereby he was appointed commander of all formations. What does this really mean? What does this order convey?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This order, it has not been worded very accurately when the order "all armed formations" doesn't exist and the commander of all armed formations does not exist in our organisational system. This is not valid, either formally or legally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But it is an order issued by the supreme command. The supreme command must be knowing what it is ordering. Did he become superior to the TO? Did he become superior to the combat units of the MUP? Did he become superior to the combat units of HVO? Did he become superior to the combat units of TO? That's what I want to find out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The supreme command, Your Honour, yes, as an institution, but the one who wrote this, who issued this order, the name and surname, initials, you can see, there is a person who writes out the order. The person who prints the order, he doesn't necessarily interpret the order of the supreme command, so he can but he --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that order, were all armed formations subordinated to Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give me an example? Did Mr. Delalic ask anything from you when he became commander of the tactical group, any material or technical means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this was one of the first misunderstandings we had. I'm saying this with reservation. That is a misunderstanding with Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It has to be obeyed. If there was any confusion, did you ask for clarification from the chief commander, from the supreme commander, what this order really signified? You haven't followed what I said. This is an order of the supreme commander, General Delalic. It had to be obeyed. If you thought there was some confusion because the order had been inaccurately worded, did you ask for any clarification from the supreme commander what he meant by "all formations"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that the municipal staff had received more specific appointments by Mr. Delalic from Sarajevo, I think so. I cannot remember the date when he received this, but I think we got clarification, we in the municipal staff, as to these questions of all formations. I think that the problem had been settled, but I can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would not like to interfere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Why don't you ask what was meant by "all formations"? You see, as I said, there were three forces, the main forces. I'm leaving out HOS, et cetera. There was the TO; it had certain combat units. You had the HVO; it had certain combat units. You had MUP; it had their own combat units. When the supreme commander says "all formations," what was that really meant to be? Was the TO staff entirely placed under the command of General Delalic or not? He said there was some confusion, the order was not clear. Then the TO must have sought clarification from the supreme commander that we don't understand the import of this order. Please tell us what is really intended to be conveyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this question was already asked to General Divjak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: And General Divjak gave the same reply and said it was inaccurate. But it is an order of the supreme commander, it has to be obeyed, and if it can't be obeyed in its present form, then some clarification must have been sought from someone, at least from the supreme commander, "We don't understand this order. Please tell us what you really mean."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And this witness has just told you, as well as the previous one, when there was this disagreement over the gun, Sultan. I'm just trying to explain that after their request on the 8th of August, the supreme command again issued an order, to which it says, clearly, that he was just the commander of Tactical Group 1. You have that other document in the evidence. I don't know exactly what happened from one day to the next, but what the witness has just said is clear. They noticed the confusion. Then a new order came dated the 8th of August from which it can clearly be seen that Zejnil Delalic was just commander of Tactical Group 1. I have tried to find it, but as this matter arose suddenly, I can't remember exactly who witnessed. I think it was a question addressed to the expert witness Vejzagic. If I've managed to be of assistance, I'm very glad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, tell me, please, in addition to this unit Gajret, which was subordinated to Commander Polutak, did any units from Konjic during the Operation JUG come under the command of other tactical groups within the framework of the operation to lift the blockade of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. One such unit was subordinated to Tactical Group 2, the command of which was on Mount Igman. I personally took such a unit there upon orders received from the supreme command, and I led the unit to Mount Igman following orders, to be more precise, to the municipality of Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cerovac, you have already testified before this Trial Chamber that the order for the formation of the Gajret unit, which was subordinated to Tactical Group 1 was issued by your commander Esad Ramic. Tell me, please, when you received a request from the supreme command to transfer a part of your forces under the command of the Tactical Group, who would issue the order on sending units or parts of units from Konjic to the areas under the control of the Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The decision was taken by me and Commander Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that we have heard that your front-lines were about 70 to 100 kilometres long and that, as testified by you and previous witnesses, a part of the forces were sent and subordinated to tactical groups, who was in charge of the remaining units in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The staff, the commander of the municipal staff. There was no interruption in the functioning of the system of control and command in the municipal staff, regardless of the fact that a unit was placed under the command of the Tactical Group. There was continuity all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But units which, under order of the commander, were sent to the area of Tactical Group 1 or Tactical Group 2, who were they subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the commanders of Tactical Group 1 and Tactical Group 2. In this case, to the commander of Tactical Group 1 and, in the second case, to commander of Tactical Group 2, Mr. Nijetovic (phoen).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cerovac, tell me, please, as you have explained that you participated in the take-over of the Celebici barracks, do you know, as a member of the staff and as the chief of staff, what facilities existed within these barracks? What were the main purposes for which it served?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew from the very second half of the 80's what the purpose of these barracks was. It is a typical facility of the former Yugoslav People's Army. The purpose of it was to store military reserves. The focus in this case was on storage of fuel, because there were large containers and some material which were concealed in the tunnel. Obviously, this facility was not being used for its proper function.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that after combat operations in Donje Selo and Bradina, a certain number of persons were brought to this facility, persons who had participated in those operations or who had been carrying arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how that prison in Celebici came into being? Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only prison that existed within Konjic municipality was a prison housed in the basement. There were two rooms within the basement of the MUP building. There were some detentions, people held there, after the deblocking, but there wasn't enough room, so a technical decision was taken, a decision out of necessity. When I say "necessity," I mean that the building of the ministry of the interior, the MUP, and the building of the TO staff headquarters, were right next to one another, and that is where I regularly went to work before the war. They were the first two facilities to be directly hit by 115 millimetre shells.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. You said that the decision was taken. Who took that decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The institution that was responsible for that decision, the ministry, the MUP, it was in its building, in its premises.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the town of Konjic, except for classrooms, was there any other facilities where a large number of people could be placed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, there were none. In the town itself, we had this big problem already at the end of April. The first refugees reached our city, non-Serb population expelled from the village of Bijela, Jocinica, Gajic, Gacici (phoen). Most of these cities were torched, Glavaticevo and others. These were local refugees, if I can put it this way, and they were put up with friends in collective centres, and then we had an even bigger problem, a very large wave of non-Serb of refugees expelled by Serb forces from eastern Herzegovina or the area of the municipality of Nevesinje, for we border with that municipality of Nevesinje, and I personally welcomed them. These were refugees from Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Cerovac. I think that is sufficient. The Trial Chamber is familiar with these facts. These tens of thousands of people coming, where did you accommodate them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you regarding a couple of large groups that I'm familiar with. One group was put up in a kindergarten, Zuleha Begeta; another group in the basement of the machine factory in Konjic; a third group of refugees in the Boy Scouts building; a fourth group in the premises close to the town of Konjic in the village of Podorasac; in the premises of the company of Bojica and also in schools. Many refugees were put up in schools.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it is clear from your testimony that the town of Konjic had no facilities for the accommodation of large groups of people. My next question is, Mr. Cerovac, do you personally know who brought people to the Celebici barracks after they were detained, taken into custody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As in my previous testimony, I said that police forces participated in these operations in Donje Selo, in particular, and also in the region of Bradina. In deblocking the road, police forces from the municipality of Hadzici participated, the MUP of Hadzici. The people were taken into custody by police forces and by TO units in the month of May when these operations took place. There was no established military police whose task this would have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cerovac, do you have any knowledge as to which forces secured the Celebici barracks where the prison was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was a MUP unit. It was called the "Special MUP Unit," and there were members of the HVO and their military police, and later on, the TO as well late in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the joint command, did you have any knowledge about the formation of a commission which was to interrogate these persons and establish their responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was just informed about it because my work was specific and I spent a lot of time in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was the president of that commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The president of the military investigating commission was Mr. Goran Lokas, who was a jurist by training.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who were the members of that commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't have to know all the names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I shall do my best to tell you all the names. I will probably remember. In terms of structure, I know that the majority of members of the commission represented the MUP. MUP representatives were the most numerous because they are familiar with the interrogations procedure, so that they were the most numerous in that commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did the TO staff appoint one or several members of that commission? Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they appointed Mr. Sacir Pajic at the beginning of July, I think, in the first half of July, we withdrew him for the purpose of forming and organising military police detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who appointed him to that commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Generally speaking, it was the joint command. Generally speaking, all of them, including Goran Lokas and Mr. Pajic were appointed by the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What about the members coming from MUP? Who appointed them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only their superior, that is, the chief of the police station, chief of the MUP station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of your personal knowledge, could you say whether Zejnil Delalic was authorised and whether, as far as you know, did he ever appoint any single member of this commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. What I do know, that is, the time Mr. Delalic -- while Mr. Delalic was working and living there during 1992, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, would this be a convenient time for the break so that I can continue after the lunch break with this witness? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We will assemble at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly inform the witness he is still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
