utterances.text: Yes, I think I saw such documents at the beginning of the month of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you recollect how many orders you saw regarding Mr. Delalic's appointment as Tactical Group 1 commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I couldn't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He said at the beginning of August. I'm sorry. It's not at the beginning of July. It's at the beginning of August that he saw those orders, at the beginning of the month of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, you would agree with me that the supreme command could have appointed a Tactical Group commander to have authority over all units falling within the authority of the supreme command? Let me clarify. I am not asking you for your opinion as to what the supreme command did, since you're not a member of the supreme command. I'm just questioning you about something you said in direct. You would agree with me that the supreme command could have appointed a tactical group commander to have authority over all units that fell within the authority of the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your wording of your question, the way you formulated it, is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's a hypothetical statement, your thoughts, whatever way you look at it. I agree that it could or might not, but it's not directed at any particular situation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There could have been some appointments, as the Prosecutor states, of all the formations in the case of Jablanica and Dreznica. This could have occurred through ignorance of someone belonging to the staff or of someone who was there. When I saw such an order, I realised that this was a question of military ignorance, especially when the words "all armed formations" are used, all armed formations in Javica (phoen), Jablanica and Konjic, where the MUP, the HVO and the TO. The HVO was never subordinated to the command of the formation of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I think you've explained that. My specific question was: Certainly, you would agree that the supreme command have the authority to appoint a Tactical Group commander as a superior authority over all units falling within the authority of the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Yes. This question is very simple. The supreme command could place --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question is very simple. The supreme command was authorised to form tactical groups and to order the municipal staff to subordinate the Tactical Group for certain tasks in a given area and for a given period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, who were members of the Tactical Group 1 staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which period do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: The period from June until November. If you want to make a distinction, you can tell us who was a member of the staff when Mr. Polutak was commander and who was a member of the staff when Mr. Delalic was commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Mr. Mustafa Polutak was commander, I know him personally, and the chief of staff was Mr. Pelica (phoen), former officer of the JNA, and he contacted him on matters of artillery. During the TG-1 when Mr. Delalic was in charge, I don't know who was in the staff. I don't know much about their structure and the names of the persons involved. This was not my duty to know them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: No, it is not your duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified, and you can correct me if I am wrong, that the purpose of Tactical Group 1 was to lift the siege of Sarajevo and the purpose of the JUG Operation was to lift the siege of Sarajevo. My question is: Is it the case that all the troops from Konjic who participated in JUG 92 were subordinated to either Tactical Group 1 or Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The units which the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of Konjic subordinated to TG-1, once they arrived in Pazaric, they automatically subordinated to TG-1. The units which we sent to the zone of responsibility of TG-2, when we brought them there, they are subordinated to the commander of TG-2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just before you start the next question, there was Operation Oganj going on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Operation Oganj also was going on about the same time. When were the troops from this Oganj Operation withdrawn from there? See, there were two operations, TG-1 lifting the siege of Sarajevo; Oganj to liberate the Borci and the surrounding area. Certain troops of yours were committed to the Oganj Operation. Certain troops were committed to Sarajevo. When were the troops committed to the Oganj Operation withdrawn from there? TG-1 is not concerned with the Oganj Operation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: TG-1 had no connection with the Borci Operation. Borci Operation was carried out on order of the command of Sarajevo in order to relieve pressure on our forces in Sarajevo. Our task was to make it easier for our defence forces who were around Sarajevo to draw some troops to our side and to liberate some of the barracks to reach the Nevesinje Ploca.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Troops which were committed to the Oganj Operation, were they withdrawn from there? Because one of the witnesses has said that they didn't want the Borci area to remain undefended because they were afraid there might be an attack on Konjic from the Borci side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Operation Oganj lasted a little over the month. Of course, all the units were not withdrawn from the operation. Some of them remained to carry on daily activities and we continued until the signing of the Dayton Agreements. We continued our combat activity for the liberation of the country. This is quite normal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: When you talk about all formations, you also have to take into consideration troops considered for Oganj.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, let me go back for a minute. Is it the case when you stated in direct examination that you led a group that was subordinated to Tactical Group 2, do you mean that you just physically led the group there or do you mean that you, for some period of time, were subordinated to Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Initially, I took the group to the Trnovo area. Before then, I went to the command of TG-2 to find what the tasks to accomplish were and to the commander of the unit, Mr. Zlatan Regic (phoen), who was appointed commander of the unit, to give Mr. Regic instructions for his further work.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Was this during the time that you were chief of staff for the TO, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, you mentioned before that the Gijret unit, for a time, was subordinate to Tactical Group 1. For how long a time was the Gijret unit subordinate to Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly how long this subordination lasted. I don't think it lasted long. Once the tasks were taken care of, they returned to Konjic and became a part of the municipal staff again. So once they returned to Konjic, they were no longer subordinated to the command of the TG-2.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm correct that the Oganj Operation -- well, let me go on, actually. Sir, were there ever any soldier units from Konjic who were subordinate to Mr. Delalic when he was commander of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kindly repeat the question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: When Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1, were there any units that were subordinated to Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Troops from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Troops from Konjic, yes, I'm sorry. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already answered the question a long time ago. This was on the order of Mr. Ramic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He, in fact, yesterday mentioned the name of the leader of the troops which were committed from Konjic to TG-1 when (inaudible) was the commander? (Judge Jan's mic not on)

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can I just ask you, sir, to potentially repeat what you stated before? How many soldiers and for what unit were subordinated to Mr. Delalic when he was commander of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You asked me the question as to the number of soldiers, soldiers who belonged to a unit called Gijret. There were about 200 soldiers, but army as such, not. The terminology is wrong. "Army" is wrong to use. "Soldiers" is the right term.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Sir, didn't you just say that the Gijret unit was no longer subordinate to Tactical Group 1 when Mr. Delalic was commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The task was completed with regard to TG-1, Tactical Group 1. The commander was Mr. Polutak and you keep mentioning Mr. Delalic. The unit of Gijret went back to Konjic and automatically returns to its own organisational formation, structure. So do not mention Mr. Delalic with reference to TG-1 and Gijret. This unit was subordinate to Mr. Mustafa Polutak in Pazaric.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, I understood your testimony about that, and that's why --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you want me to continue, Your Honour or do you want me to stop?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let's get this issue clear because it's still not satisfactory. What happened when Delalic was appointed to Tactical Group 1? Was he not assigned any men to work with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course he needed to have men to work with him. There was a staff up there, the brain behind it all. I'm not familiar with that staff and I do not know how Mr. Delalic organised that. Those are his responsibilities. At the time, I didn't have any right to interfere. I had my permanent, regular activities in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Learned counsel is asking, how many units from Konjic TO were placed under the command of Zejnil Delalic when he became the commander of TG-1? How many units from TO were detached and sent to TG-1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To TG-1?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While Mr. Zejnil Delalic was commander, as far as I know, not a single unit, not a single unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: So, sir, if there is a chart that shows there were between 3 and 500 soldiers attached to Tactical Group 1 during the time that Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1, that chart would be incorrect, according to your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You keep saying that I said that 200 soldiers were subordinated to Mr. Zejnil Delalic. That is not correct. I have just said that not a single unit, no fixed number of soldiers, as far as I know during the existence of Tactical Group 1 while Mr. Zejnil Delalic was commander, were sent by order of the TO commander to that Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose we can end here and continue by 10.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of May, 1998 at 10.00 a.m. 25
